summary: In this tutorial, you learn how to use command-line arguments in C programs using the GCC compiler on Ubuntu OS. The main function takes two arguments: `argc` for the number of command-line arguments and `argv` as an array of strings containing the actual arguments. `argc` includes the program name as the first argument, and `argv[0]` represents the program name. Subsequent elements in `argv` contain the actual command-line arguments passed to the program. The tutorial demonstrates compiling and running a sample program that prints the number of arguments and their values. For example, passing "sunday monday tuesday" results in four arguments being printed. The tutorial covers the basics of using command-line arguments in C programs and provides a link to the full video for further learning.
